mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY growth > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5% MoM does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) over 3 months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST decline > 5% over 3 months does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 1% MoM does not correlate with subsequent economic strength.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase > 200,000 does not correlate with subsequent economic strength.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening consumer sector, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% MoM and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with subsequent economic strength.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) coupled with an increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals a shift towards accommodative monetary policy in an inflationary environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.25% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with subsequent market strength.
